sources.title: Dealing with Infinite Loops, Underestimation, and Overestimation of Depth-First Proof-Number Search
sources.read_scope: PublisherPDF retrieved; abstract andmethodspages108-111 inspected, no independent implementation/benchmarkreproduction.
sources.summary: Proof/disproof threshold methods need special treatment of cycles and shared descendants. The paper distinguishes loop avoidance from undercounting and duplicate overcounting; it proposes threshold control and source-node detection. These mechanisms are not implemented in our BFS prototype.
sources.next_use: Before changing frontier priority, trace actual repeated/state-expansion work on root1/27; keep independent finite-rank certificates and existing semantic/history guard. Do not treat ordinary graph reuse or retained thresholds as DFPN.

sources.title: The Graph History Interaction Problem
sources.read_scope: Authorprojectpage andpublicationmetadata read; linked2004PDF returned404, no fullpaperreadclaim.
sources.summary: The same position can behave differently after different paths. Our history quotient is a limited sufficient condition for finite winning witnesses, not a general GHI solution.
